title: Repeat-the-same-mistake loop (anti-illusion test), MAIN and LMS
brief_expectation: A student who keeps choosing one wrong idea on 3 items over 2 sessions must (a) keep low unassisted mastery, (b) have that misconception counted and confirmed on 2+ items, (c) get a different next activity than a control after the 2nd or 3rd repeat.

conclusion: The LAM only half survives the anti-illusion test. The mastery half is real in both trees: 6 cold wrongs on one idea leave unassisted mastery at 0.02 (control 0.98), and 2 hinted rights do not lift it (assisted 0.928 vs unassisted 0.02). On MAIN, nextActivity sends S back to X when X's dependent Z is next (prerequisite[X] vs next for C), and flipping S to right flips it back. The misconception half does not exist as a loop. MAIN: the misconceptionId is written to the ledger by 3 emitters, then foldAnswer drops it. No ConceptState field, no exported function, no registry counts it; same-idea vs scattered-guess students fold byte-identical; decide() ignores history on a wrong answer and replays 'first miss, follow-up' on the 7th identical miss; nextActivity fires after ONE wrong (0.118), so repetition is not what triggers it; once the review is due (3 days) S and C get the identical review[X]; the prerequisite Y is never reached because unassisted belief is not propagated and nothing asks Y cold. LMS: the server fold is correct, and the homework path counts the label (S times 6 vs U times 1, D scattered, C/F none), but the likely list has no threshold (a single slip is listed with the repeater), tutor ledger misconceptionIds and the student's own practice picks are never counted (0 rows each), concept_state has no misconception column, the chapter pick uses blended mastery (hinted answers lift it 0.02 to 0.209), and practice is order by random() from a student-independent pool (X share 0.487 vs control 0.50). The only misconception-targeted next action is the teacher's manual send_practice. Aarav's definition ('different next activity because of the repeated wrong idea') is met by neither tree: both differ by S vs C only through the mastery number. Score for this loop: MAIN about 2/5 (code and mastery signal exist; the misconception link is absent), LMS about 3/5 for the human-in-the-loop homework path only. Not tested: re-take attempts in LMS (the code reads only the latest attempt per assignment, 0040:533) and the real classroom wiring of nextActivity, which I did not trace.
probe_bugs: Three probe issues, all fixed. (1) First comparison used JSON of the whole NextActivity, which differs trivially in the 'because' day count; changed to compare the activity itself (kind plus outcome ids). (2) The k-wise test originally used a fixed now and was confounded by a due review; changed to now = 1 hour after the k-th wrong, and split 'fires by k=3' (pass) from the stricter 'only on repetition' (fail). (3) My LMS 'X share > 0.5' assertion passed by chance at 0.52; replaced by an S-vs-C share difference. I also dropped one assertion I invented (prerequisite blended belief should not exceed the prior) and kept it as a note only. LMS PractiseNow logic is a verbatim copy of home.tsx:157 because it is inline in a React component, not an importable function. The hinted answers on LMS were injected as ledger rows (the homework path has no help ladder; the tutor's rows reach the same table). No fault in the probes remains known.

title: Guessing vs knowing, and hint-dependence (assisted vs unassisted mastery)
brief_expectation: One lucky right must not make a skill mastered. Rights given only with heavy help (rungs 5-8) must leave UNASSISTED mastery low and discount blended mastery. credit(rung k) <= credit(rung k-1). Mastered needs unassisted AND spaced AND a different item. Repeats of the same item are not independent evidence. Wheel-spin and hint-abuse detectors must fire on constructed sequences AND something must consume them.

conclusion: MAIN has the right arithmetic and the rung and mastered rules hold on every constructed stream. title: Fold determinism: replay, duplicates, disorder, batch splits, version migration (MAIN)
brief_expectation: The fold must be a pure function of the ledger. Folding twice, with duplicated event ids, in shuffled order, or split into any batches (fold(A+B) == fold(A) then fold(B) with the cursor) must give identical models. An older MODEL_VERSION must migrate without losing evidence. 20k events must fold in reasonable time.
trees_tested: MAIN (C:/Users/Ashish Sharma/curie, branch phase3-completion). Static reads only of LMS think.ts (LMS tree not exercised).

checks.name: Controls: purity, non-vacuous model, comparator sensitivity
checks.expected: Same ledger folded twice gives an identical, non-trivial model; a flipped answer, a dropped event or a reversed session is detected.
checks.observed: Rebuild twice: equal, 221 states, 163 observations. Flipped answer: 10 fields differ (max 0.52). Dropped event: 7 fields. Reversed session: 265 fields. Deep-frozen inputs: no mutation, no throw.
checks.root_cause: fold.ts:76-118 builds new objects and has no clock or randomness; grep for Math.random/Date.now in learner-model and knowledge-graph src found none.

checks.name: Idempotence (same batch twice; whole history re-fed onto the finished model)
checks.expected: Folding the same events again changes nothing.
checks.observed: 8 seeds x 5 sessions x 40 events. Per-session fold twice: 8/8 equal (0 fields differ). Whole history re-fed: 8/8 equal.
checks.root_cause: The cursor check at fold.ts:94 and behindCursor at fold.ts:134-141 skip anything at or behind foldedThrough.

checks.name: Batch-split equivalence at EVERY boundary, random splits, per-event calls, empty batches
checks.expected: fold(A+B) equals fold(A) then fold(B), at any cut including mid-session.
checks.observed: 442 two-way boundaries over 3 seeds (about 148 events each): 0 mismatches. 200 random multi-way splits: 0 mismatches. 20k one-call-per-event: equal to the batched model. An empty batch before every event: equal.
checks.root_cause: fold.ts:70-74 carries help in flight inside the model, so a split no longer hides a helped row from the next answer.

checks.name: Duplicate event suppression (same id, same seq)
checks.expected: A duplicate or a redelivered batch is ignored.
checks.observed: 8 seeds: every event doubled adjacent, then the whole batch redelivered: 8/8 identical to the clean rebuild.
checks.root_cause: Suppression is by cursor position (fold.ts:94), not by id.

checks.name: Duplicate event id re-sent under a NEW seq; ledger replayCounters with a duplicated id
checks.expected: A repeated event id is counted once.
checks.observed: The fold counted an id twice when seq changed: 77 observations became 85, 74 fields differ. replayCounters on a doubled ledger: answered 38 became 76. Neither fold.ts nor replay.ts:83-127 looks at event.id.
checks.root_cause: Id idempotence lives only in the DB: ledger_event.id is the primary key (0006_ledger.sql:58) and unique(session_id,seq) (0006:115). Through the DB a duplicate cannot reach the fold, so this is a missing defence in depth, not a reachable bug today.
suggested_fixes: In foldSession, keep a bounded set of recent event ids (or store the last folded event id in the cursor) and skip repeats.
Dedupe by id in replayCounters.

checks.name: Order independence: shuffled events inside a session
checks.expected: Shuffled input gives the same model (or at least no silent loss).
checks.observed: 8 seeds, one batch per session, shuffled: 8/8 differ from the sorted fold. 102-144 of about 105-165 observations silently lost per seed, up to 194 states missing, 224-533 fields differ.
checks.root_cause: foldSession neither sorts by seq nor rejects out-of-order input. It documents 'ordered by seq ascending' at fold.ts:49, and an event behind the cursor is dropped with no signal (fold.ts:94). Callers sort (rebuildModel.ts:~229), but nothing enforces it.
suggested_fixes: Sort events by seq inside foldSession, or throw / return a 'dropped N' count when an event is behind the cursor.
Keep a per-session set of folded seqs so a late lower seq is folded instead of dropped (a rebuild is then needed only for cross-session order).

checks.name: Late arrival: seq chunks out of order, one late event, and older sessions delivered late
checks.expected: Every event is counted whatever the delivery order, or the loss is detected.
checks.observed: Chunks of 8 delivered in shuffled order: 58-94 of 122-155 observations lost per seed (8/8 seeds). One answer delayed past its successor: lost in 133/133 trials (4 seeds). Sessions shuffled: 60-141 of 147-180 observations lost (8/8 seeds). No error, no counter.
checks.root_cause: The cursor is a high-water mark (fold.ts:134-141). Anything at or behind it is lost for good. The ledger's own comment says rows 'arrive out of order from an offline outbox' (rebuildModel.ts, on 0006). The outbox is FIFO (outbox.ts:244), so it is reachable mainly through multi-device use, a held session-started (ledgerSync.ts:~150-176) or a retry. There is no server fold in MAIN to notice any of it.
suggested_fixes: Track folded (sessionId,seq) pairs instead of one high-water mark, or mark the model dirty whenever an event arrives behind the cursor and rebuild from zero.
Make the fold return the list of skipped events so the caller can log and trigger a rebuild.

checks.expected: Session order comes from a server clock, as the cursor docs claim.
checks.observed: A sitting stamped 3 days early, folded in arrival order: 27 of 104 observations lost (77 kept).
checks.root_cause: types.ts:167-171 and fold.ts:30 say started_at is a server clock and 'phones lie', but ledgerSync.ts:169 writes `started_at: e.at` (the device clock) and 0011_close_session_once.sql:51 admits it. The cursor orders on the clock it says it cannot trust.

checks.observed: Model damaged by shuffled sessions: 18 observations. Rebuild from the sorted ledger: 151, and a second rebuild is identical.
checks.root_cause: The ledger is the record and the fold is deterministic on sorted input. But no code calls a rebuild automatically on a skipped event.

The help for the live sitting is erased, so deriveRung sees rung 0. This is the error rung.ts says nothing downstream corrects.
suggested_fixes: When every event of the batch is behind the cursor, return the model unchanged.
Only replace helpInFlight when session.id is at or ahead of the cursor session, or keep a map of byAsk per session.

checks.expected: Prior history survives.
checks.observed: v2 model with 221 states and 104 observations, folded with one new session: 146 states and 31 observations remained. The history was wiped and replaced by that one session.
checks.root_cause: fold.ts:65-68 starts any model of another version from emptyModel() by design. The one caller, learnerModel.ts:192-199, runs migrateModel first, so the wipe is guarded in the app. But the function is a foot-gun for any new caller, such as a server fold.
suggested_fixes: Throw (or return a tagged result) on a version mismatch instead of silently emptying.

checks.name: Migrate(v2 or v1) then continue equals a fresh rebuild from the ledger
checks.expected: Equal to a rebuild, so no gap in spaced review.
checks.observed: 3 seeds, 221/221/146 states: 70-94 fields differ. Mastery and unassistedMastery max diff 0 (identical). Only the spaced-review fields differ: box (14 states), nextReviewAt (21), lastExposedAt (12), lastRetrievedAt (17), retrievalCount (17). Outcomes with a review date: migrated 26/35/30 against rebuilt 39/40/38, about a quarter missing. v1 (no masteredAt/coldWins): 93 fields differ. The v1 hint-credit arithmetic difference could not be reproduced without old code (inconclusive).
checks.root_cause: migrate.ts:12-14 documents that a migration cannot undo the old arithmetic or build boxes. migrateModel does not replay the ledger, and the continued fold sets boxes only on the next exposure (memory.ts onExposure). 'Revisit later' is therefore silently missing for those outcomes. The production path rebuilds, but rebuildModel.ts:34 and :159-173 refuse more than 1000 events or sittings, and learnerModel.ts:154-170 then falls back to migrateModel.
suggested_fixes: Page the ledger read instead of refusing past 1000 rows.
Backfill box and nextReviewAt in migrateModel from lastPracticedAt and lastUnassistedSuccessAt.

checks.name: Rebuild path equals a fresh rebuild
checks.expected: A rebuild from the full ledger over an old-version model equals a fresh rebuild.
checks.observed: v2 model plus the full ledger through foldSession: identical to a fresh rebuild (0 fields differ).
checks.root_cause: fold.ts:65-68 empties an old-version model first, so the fold has nothing stale to carry.

checks.name: Performance: 20k events
checks.expected: Reasonable time (pre-registered: under 10 s, and not quadratic).
checks.observed: 20,220 events (200 sittings x 100): 5.0 s and 6.1 s on two runs. The 5k subset took 1.2-1.7 s, so 4x events cost 3.5-4x time, linear. Rerun identical. 20k one call per event: 2.9-4.7 s, equal to batched. Worst case, 20k events over all 371 graph nodes: 10.5-11.4 s. Timings are noisy because other sessions share the machine. About 250 microseconds per event, which is roughly 25x the cost on a 371-node map when every node is touched.
checks.root_cause: Each answer copies the states map and rebuilds `before` over all states (fold.ts:246, :276-277), so cost grows with touched states. It is fine at 371 nodes, but a student across all 26 maps would be slower. The wide case was not run on a larger graph.

conclusion: For sorted input the fold is solid. It is pure and idempotent, a redelivered batch is ignored, and a split at all 442 boundaries (plus 200 random splits and per-event calls) gives identical models. Rebuilding old-version models from the ledger gives the same model, and 20k events take about 5 s and scale linearly. The brief's order and duplicate guarantees do not hold: the cursor is a high-water mark, so any event or sitting that arrives after something later is lost silently (58-141 of about 120-180 observations lost per seed when delivery is shuffled, and a single late answer was lost in 133 of 133 trials). Three more defects: redelivering an old session erases the live sitting's help and manufactures unassisted mastery (0 observations became 1, mastery 0.50 became 0.78); the DB cursor is still 2-part while the fold needs 3, and a 2-part cursor re-counted 22 of 66 observations; and learning_session.started_at is the phone's clock (ledgerSync.ts:169), not the server clock the cursor docs assume. Nothing in MAIN writes learner_model or concept_state, so no server fold exists to repair any of this. migrateModel loses no numbers, but a migrated model has no spaced-review boxes, about a quarter of review dates missing against a rebuild, and the rebuild fallback is refused past 1000 events or sittings. Score for fold determinism: 3/5 (excellent when ordered, no protection when not).
probe_bugs: One early probe bug: afterAll overwrote the shared JSON when I re-ran with -t, so I re-ran the whole file and the numbers above come from that full rerun (they match run 1 except timings). The 'late event' and 'shuffled' tests deliberately feed input that violates the documented 'ordered by seq' contract, so they measure what the fold does with it, not a caller bug. Mastery and unassistedMastery diffs were measured by an inline diff() comparing numbers with strict equality. The v1/v2 blobs are the real v3 fold with fields stripped, so the old hint-credit arithmetic was not reproduced and is reported inconclusive. The wide-graph perf test used only the 371-node class10-science map.
suggested_fixes: Fold late data instead of dropping it: track folded (sessionId, seq) or flag the model dirty and rebuild from zero when an event arrives behind the cursor (fold.ts:94, :134-141).
Return the model unchanged when a whole batch is behind the cursor, and do not overwrite helpInFlight (fold.ts:120).
Make the DB cursor match the fold: add a session id column to learner_model or drop sessionId from the key (0013_learner_model.sql:78-79, types.ts:181-185).
Stamp learning_session.started_at server-side (ledgerSync.ts:169).
Add a server fold to MAIN (lms-brain think.ts is the reference), and give rebuildModel.ts:159 a (started_at, id) order and paging past 1000 rows.
Make foldSession throw on a version mismatch instead of silently emptying (fold.ts:65-68), and backfill review boxes in migrateModel.
Normalise startedAt to canonical ISO text inside foldSession.

The server fold (LMS lms-brain think.ts) equals a replay, is restartable, persists what the model knows, and is run by something on the hosted project.

checks.observed: Tampered S1 row (mastery 0.01) restored exactly. S2 concept_state and learner_model deleted: 56 rows rebuilt, max delta 1.9e-8.

checks.name: E15 something on the hosted project runs the fold
checks.expected: a pg_cron job, Edge Function or workflow that calls think/lms-brain
checks.observed: cron jobs in migrations: purge-old-ledger (0009), lms-finalize-tests (0030:345), neither folds. Edge functions: [relay]. think() callers: tools/lms-demo/src/server.ts:199,279 and seed.ts:357 only (local PGlite). think.ts:20-22 says 'On the hosted project nothing runs it yet'.
checks.root_cause: The server fold exists as tested code and is wired only into the local demo server. On hosted Supabase concept_state is never written, so the teacher analytics read an empty table. MAIN has no server fold either (no insert into concept_state anywhere in apps, packages, tools).
suggested_fixes: Run think from an Edge Function triggered after submit, or add a ledger_event insert trigger/queue; schedule a nightly reconcile via pg_cron

checks.name: E16 think() writes learner_model.purge_safe_before
checks.expected: non-null after a fold (migration 0021 comment: 'written by the server fold')
checks.observed: purge_safe_before=null after think(). The only writer is nobody. 0021:141-144 says the purge deletes no events while it is null.
checks.root_cause: Retention is deliberately disarmed until the fold marks what it has read. The fold never marks it, so school ledgers grow without bound, against the 90-day policy.
suggested_fixes: Set purge_safe_before to the last folded session in think()

checks.name: E17 armed purge then think(): does the fold forget purged evidence
checks.expected: concept_state unchanged after purge + think
checks.observed: With purge_safe_before armed by hand and the oldest 3 sessions aged out: purge removed 9 events and 3 sessions. think() rebuilt from the remaining 16. S6 commutative-multiplication observations 13 -> 8, mastery unchanged only because recent evidence dominates.
checks.root_cause: think() deletes and rebuilds from the ledger alone (think.ts:124), so the moment retention is armed (E16) it silently discards counts and older evidence. 'Rebuild' and 'purge' are incompatible without a stored snapshot.
suggested_fixes: Keep the previous model as the fold's start and fold only post-cursor events, or snapshot before purge

checks.name: E18 overlapping think() for one child
checks.expected: all runs succeed, rows correct
checks.observed: 3 concurrent runs for one child: 2 rejected with 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint concept_state_pkey'. Final rows equal the good set.
checks.root_cause: think.ts:124 delete and :127 insert are separate query() calls with no transaction or per-user lock, so two hand-ins interleave. In demo server.ts:199 the await sits in the request path, so a student's submit can return an error after the answer was saved.
suggested_fixes: Wrap delete+insert+learner_model upsert in one transaction with pg_advisory_xact_lock(user)

checks.name: imports the older learner-model
checks.expected: lms-brain folds with the current tutor model
checks.observed: think.ts:1-2 imports from @ai-tutor/learner-model, which in the LMS tree resolves to packages/learner-model with MODEL_VERSION=1 (8 source files differ from MAIN; memory.ts, mastered.ts, migrate.ts, next.ts absent). MAIN also has packages/tutor-control; LMS has none.
checks.root_cause: The 'one idea of what a child knows' comment (think.ts:8-12) was true at a695b1d and is false today: 159 commits on MAIN (B4, B6, B8, F1-F3) never reached the lms branch.

conclusion:
Short answer: the LAM is not one brain today. It is two folds that agree on the base and disagree on everything added since 2026-09-25, and the server fold is real code that nothing hosted runs.

What I ran. One deterministic stream of 7 students and 119 events: hinted and cold answers, misconception ids, retries, real LMS homework payloads, 5 to 20 days. I folded it through MAIN's learner-model (v3) and the LMS tree's (v1) and compared them concept by concept. I then ran lms-brain's think() against PGlite with the real migrations.

1. Same stream, different beliefs. Across 80 concept pairs, 31 shared-field differences, 0 unexplained. 19 are spaced-review dates and counts that exist only in v3. 12 are belief differences: the help discount (B4), where a right answer at rung 3 moves mastery 0.7 as far in MAIN (ratio measured 0.7000), and the retry rule, where an attempt-2 answer counts as help in MAIN only. Worst gaps: a hint-only child shows mastery 0.726 in MAIN and 0.959 in LMS, with zero cold answers. A retry child shows unassisted mastery 0.209 vs 0.453. The LMS cannot represent box, masteredAt or review due at all. Control students with no hints or retries match exactly, so the harness is not noise.

2. lms-brain is a correct server fold but not a deployed one. Stored concept_state equals a ledger replay to 2e-8 for all 80 rows, a re-run changes nothing, a tampered or deleted model is healed, and a back-dated session folds in order. Its own 11 tests pass. It rebuilds the whole ledger every call rather than moving a cursor. But nothing hosted calls it. The hosted cron jobs are the purge and the test finalizer, there is one Edge Function (relay), and the only think() callers are the local demo server and the seed script. So concept_state is never written on the hosted project, and MAIN does not write it either.

3. Defects found in the fold itself. It never writes purge_safe_before, so the 90-day ledger retention stays disarmed. If someone arms it, rebuild-from-ledger loses evidence (observations 13 to 8 in my run). Overlapping runs for one child fail with duplicate-key errors (2 of 3 runs).

4. Merge requirement for ONE brain. (a) Make packages/learner-model a single package: take MAIN's, which includes memory.ts, mastered.ts, migrate.ts and next.ts. The knowledge-graph content is already identical and the migrations don't collide (MAIN ends at 0020, LMS adds 0021 to 0042). (b) Add `itemId` to itemKey in fold.ts:162, or LMS homework can never reach B8 mastery (measured: 6 distinct items over 5 days, masteredAt null). (c) New migration for box, mastered_at, cold_wins, last_exposed_at and last_retrieved_at, extend think() COLUMNS, and store version 3. (d) Run think from something hosted: an Edge Function or trigger after a hand-in, plus a nightly reconcile. (e) Make think() transactional with a per-child lock, write purge_safe_before, and fold from a cursor or snapshot so retention does not erase evidence. (f) Decide where tutor-control's decide() lives, since the LMS tree has none.

Rubric for this slice. Server fold exists and matches replay: 4 as code, 2 as a product, because no student reaches it on the hosted project. One shared idea of what a child knows: 2.

conclusion: Score for this brief item: 2 of 5 on MAIN and 1 to 2 on LMS. What exists is a clean 5079-node, 6546-edge DAG that passes every integrity check, and a planner that orders a prerequisite before its dependent once the prerequisite itself has been answered. What the brief asks for does not exist. Cross-class edges: 0 of 6546, so no Class 9 node has a Class 7 ancestor and a Class 9 failure cannot be traced to a Class 7 root. Even with one injected edge on real nodes the chain still fails to trace, because of three further gaps. 1) mastery.ts:128 lowers only descendants after a wrong answer, so ancestors stay at 0.50 and the fold (device and LMS server concept_state) writes no ancestor row. 2) The plan and learnFromQuiz evidence gate admits only the answered node plus its descendants, so an unprobed ancestor can never become a step. 3) nextActivity (MAIN only) looks one hop from the next topic and only at prerequisites with cold evidence, so a root two hops away or an unasked prerequisite is skipped and the student is moved on. Placement found a hidden Class 7 root in 1 of 5 trials (same with an injected edge) and a Class 9 root in 2 of 5, which is about the rate of asking it by chance. LMS is the same or worse: it runs the same propagation through lms-brain/think.ts, has no nextActivity and no planner reading prerequisites, and libraryIndex() merges the maps with no links step. Controls: positive controls passed (descendants lowered 137/137, correct raises ancestors, direct-prerequisite nextActivity, prerequisite-before-dependent plan order, loader integrity); negative controls passed (loader rejects cycle, dangling and duplicate; no spurious prerequisite; 0 unrelated nodes moved). Probe bugs fixed: E2 first picked roots with no bank probe. Not tested: real probe selection against live students, any model call.

title: Tutor-control ladder: does the controller choose, escalate and log?
brief_expectation: decide() escalates in a fixed order on repeated wrong answers (look again, hint, answer plus why), never leaks the answer in a hint, never loops forever, is deterministic, handles "not sure", hint requests and silence, records the rung it chose, and that rung reaches the ledger as an intervened row with the reason and then the fold. A last-resort rung exists.

checks.observed: type and SQL accept it; fold ignores it (states identical with/without, fold.ts:104-107). BUT recordsFor() is called by 0 files in apps/ or packages/ outside tests; ClassRoom has 3 decide() sites (1201,1253,1430) and 5 ledger.helped writes, 0 intervened writes

checks.expected: Action.scheduleRetest read by some app/queue; the conductor that queues retests is mounted
checks.observed: scheduleRetest read by 0 files outside tutor-control; createConductor called by 0 files outside tutor-control (only conductor.ts:807 queueRetest and tests)

checks.expected: attempt count alone should escalate (attempt=9, rungSoFar=0 should not return a hint)
checks.observed: decide(attempt=9, rungSoFar=0) = hint@3 (floor only lifts to L1)
checks.root_cause: decide.ts:455-458 floorRung uses attempt only to lift 0 to 1. ClassRoom keeps rung in a React ref (rungAt) so a remount mid-question restarts the ladder. Pre-registered stricter than the design contract, so low.

checks.name: LMS has a controller (choose / escalate / log)
checks.expected: some controller exists; leak check; escalation; intervened rows
checks.observed: no packages/tutor-control; 0 decide( sites; 0 recordsFor; 0 intervened writers; 0 leak check. ClassRoom files fixed helped rungs only: ClassRoom.tsx:315 (rung 3), :762 (3 or 2 per model's 'gave'), :921 (7)
checks.root_cause: LMS branch predates tutor-control (159 commits on MAIN not in LMS). A wrong answer gets the model's reply (speakSafely, safety screen only, no leak check, ClassRoom.tsx:763) at a hardcoded rung, with no code-side escalation or cap, no reason logged.

conclusion: MAIN: the controller is real, deterministic and wired. decide() escalates in the brief's order (rethink@1, hint@3, [example@5, explain@7 where authored], reveal@8, moveOn) with a terminal cap and last resort in 40-wrong runs on every content shape. It handled 4320 grid inputs with no difference. It never leaked the literal answer in 736 adversarial actions. Silence, hint requests, shrugs and right-after-help behave as designed, and the helped rung does reach the fold (obs 0 with the rows, 1 with them lost). Three gaps are real. (1) The controller's reason is never persisted: recordsFor has no production caller and ClassRoom files only helped. (2) scheduleRetest and the conductor are consumed by no app, so the controller's retest decision does not reach a student. (3) The leak check misses Hinglish numerals and paraphrase (7/7 slipped through), and hint or explain requests never terminate. LMS has no controller at all. Scores: MAIN 3.5 of 5 (4 for choose and escalate, 2 for logging the reason and retest; call it 3 if the audit trail counts equally). LMS 0 for a controller; it only writes fixed helped rungs. Fixes, in order: wire recordsFor into ClassRoom at the three decide() sites, then consume scheduleRetest or mount the conductor, then add a request counter plus Hinglish numeral and arithmetic checks, then port tutor-control into LMS.
probe_bugs: Three probe bugs of mine, all fixed within the iteration limit. (1) I first asserted unassistedObservations==0 after a wrong>wrong>right ladder, but the first miss is a genuine cold answer at rung 0, so 1 is correct; the assertion now targets the final right answer. (2) The 'intervened moves the fold' comparison tripped on lastPracticedAt timestamps that my own seq-spaced stream shifted; those two fields are now excluded. (3) My first negative control (help rows dropped, final right at attempt 3) did not discriminate because the fold floors attempt>=2 at rung>=1 (atLeastANudge). I replaced it with a silence nudge plus hint request then a right answer at attempt 1, which does discriminate (obs 0 vs 1). Also fixed one apostrophe syntax error and one stray property. No product assertion was weakened. Existing tests: packages/tutor-control/tests 6 files, 208 tests pass. LMS probe: tutorControlDir=false (the failing assertion is the finding).
suggested_fixes: Persist the reason: in ClassRoom.tsx after each decide() at 1201, 1253 and 1430, loop recordsFor(action,{beatId}) and add a ledger.intervened(beatId, payload) writer to classLedger.ts (next to helped, classLedger.ts:588). That makes helped->intervened in order, adds the because/rung/errorClass audit row, and matches records.ts:12-22. No SQL change needed ('intervened' is already in 0006_ledger.sql:81).

Make 'revisit later' real: have ClassRoom read action.scheduleRetest and enqueue the ask id for the next session, or mount createConductor. Until then right-after-help and cold-on-weak-record retests are computed and dropped.

Close the leak gaps: normalise romanised Hindi numerals (ek, do, teen, chaar, paanch...) in leak.ts only when a hi-en ask has a numeric secret; add a tiny arithmetic evaluator that flags 'a op b' equal to a numeric secret; add a prep-time (offline, once per ask) lint in class-prep that rejects hints containing the answer by paraphrase, so runtime stays at zero model calls.

Cap request loops: count hint/explain requests per ask in ClassRoom (rungAt-style ref). After 2 repeats of the same hint, treat the next request as a wrong step (offer L5 example or L8 reveal), and persist rungAt/triesAt so a remount does not reset the ladder.
Add 'idk', 'dunno' and 'no clue' to tutor-judge DONT_KNOW (match.ts:106) so typed shrugs resolve on device instead of costing a model call.
